text: Permanent NZ GM (Mr. James O'Connor) appointed effective 1 January 2023; the Board considers the leadership transition closed and states no further changes to the NZ executive team are anticipated in the FY2023 horizon.
Approximately one third of NZ FY2022 channel revenue was delivered through a single reseller (Security Tech Inc.); diversification of the NZ customer base is a stated FY2023 priority.
NZ stabilised under new permanent leadership; all senior NZ executive roles are now permanently filled and the Board considers NZ leadership stability to be restored.

Channel partnership with Security Tech Inc. continued to be the single largest revenue driver; the Board notes the Group's reliance on this counterparty and has requested a diversification plan in FY2024.
Group revenue grew ~7% year-on-year; EBITDA margin compressed slightly versus FY2022, reflecting continued input-cost inflation partially offset by H2 pricing actions.
NZ management instability evidenced by 3 GM changes in 18 months, two critical vacancies (Sales Director; Supply Lead) filled by interim resources, and elevated attrition in mid-management.
AU executed a salary-only restructuring in Q4 — a one-off in September with a sustained run-rate reduction from October — supporting EBITDA expansion.

A pronounced revenue step-up in May 2024 followed the Smart Security campaign launch with reseller Security Tech Inc. (stronger in AU; modest in NZ); this was limited in duration, with the revenue run-rate reducing to normal once the promotional period ended.
NZ shows an EBITDA decline on slightly higher structural cost ratios and execution slippage linked to leadership churn.
NZ EBITDA-margin recovery is targeted at +120 to +180 bps by year-end if remediation milestones are achieved.
